task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Does the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes) show the largest gain in the absent player's primary play types?
Is the sample (148 spells, 11 cases) large enough to test a ranking-based redistribution claim?
How should regression to the mean and selection of absence spells be handled when measuring gains?
Which confounders (injury return, minutes changes, lineup changes) threaten attribution of gains to the absent player?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether play-type replacement similarity separates absorption from cascade when a player sits. Recorded result: mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Embiid 23-24 cascades with Reed at sim 0.94. Recorded verdict: null, failure type B_powered_null. Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED; validation status recorded as no validation recorded.

Connector absence displaced team offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021 unmatched, t=5.97; usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, n=96; vs terminal +0.0777, t=2.37, p=0.0261, n=25). Drawn from 908 player-seasons. This addresses a neighbouring question (team identity displacement), not the teammate-ranking claim.

Reproduction and null simulation of a published H1->H2 suppression excess (0.408). Under no true change the null simulation gave an excess of about 0.440, which exceeds the observed value, so the excess is attributed to regression to the mean and selection on the H2 drop. The null figure is quoted from a print string with no saved log. Sample: 1,136 caliper pairs.

Tail and null-model audit of the same published suppression excess. Reproduced excess 0.4080 (CI 0.378 to 0.438). Within-unit permutation residual +0.0054 (z 0.40). Asymmetry neg-pos 0.0176 (p=0.258). Drift-centred tail mass ratio 1.007. The apparent effect is attributed to construction, selection or labelling flaws.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type profile similarity to a teammate as the criterion for separating absorption from cascade when a player sits.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a powered null with a wrong-signed correlation. Similarity was almost always findable, so it did not discriminate. Sample size and power were not recorded, so the 'powered' label is not verified. Recorded limitation: label or classification error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Taking a published pre-to-post drop excess as evidence of a real effect without a null that accounts for regression to the mean and selection on the outcome.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: the null simulation produced an excess comparable to the observed value, so regression to the mean and selection account for the effect. Null figure is not backed by a saved log.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating the suppression excess as a real asymmetric effect.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: within-unit permutation and drift-centred tail checks show no residual effect beyond the null (z 0.40; asymmetry p=0.258).

evidence_establishes: Closest-profile similarity alone did not separate absorbed from cascaded replacements in the one retrieved test of similarity-based replacement ([prior work][prior work]), with a wrong-signed correlation.
Pre-to-post gain or drop measures conditioned on a selected trigger are vulnerable to regression to the mean and selection artifacts ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).

Team-identity displacement after connector absence can be measured against usage-matched controls with adequate matched counts in a neighbouring question ([prior work][prior work], n=96 matched pairs).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types is the most similar teammate. No retrieved record tests this ranking directly with the same measure.
Any power figure for the 148-spell, 11-case design. [prior work][prior work] has no recorded sample or power.
Whether the 'powered null' label in [prior work][prior work] is valid, given that its sample and power were not recorded and its status is recorded as inconclusive.
Whether the nulls in [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] transfer to the play-type setting, since they concern a different suppression metric.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a single-ranking claim (top-1 similarity teammate is the largest gainer). With 11 cases, a top-1 hit rate has very wide uncertainty, and the 148 spells are clustered within those cases, so effective sample size is near 11.

The retrieved similarity test ([prior work][prior work]) argues against the hypothesis as posed, but the wrong-signed result with an unverified power basis is weak evidence for rejection rather than proof.

The four proposed similarity criteria (profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) multiply the comparisons; the stated question leaves the criterion open, which allows the ranking to be chosen after seeing the data.
The same regression-to-the-mean and selection concerns recorded in the suppression-excess families apply directly to any gain measured from a selected absence spell.
uncertainties: Exact definition of 'primary types', 'largest gainer' and 'closest profile' is not given; it is not clear which measure the ranking uses.
Number of distinct absent players, and how many spells each contributes, is not stated beyond 11 cases.

Playoff data for 2025-26 was complete only from 2026-06-21, which precedes the 2026-11-01 question date, so it is usable; partial-season 2025-26 regular-season data before 2026-04-13 must be excluded.
The retrieval returned four records, not all of which bear directly on the question; the tool budget and retrieval scope may have missed other relevant records.
Whether initiator labels in the derived play-type records are reliable is not documented in the retrieved evidence.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the question looked testable on the 148-spell panel. The retrieved similarity test ([prior work][prior work]) reported a wrong-signed, null result for the closest analogue of this claim, and the regression-to-the-mean artifacts ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) show that gains measured from selected triggers are easily produced by construction. Together these lower the probability of a clean test and require a null model and a fixed criterion before any analysis, so the decision moved to do_not_proceed as posed, with a minimum viable test specified below.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases underlie 148 spells; a top-1 ranking hit rate cannot be estimated with useful precision at this case count.

Gains are measured from selected absence triggers, so regression to the mean and selection can produce a top-ranked gainer by construction (as in [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work]).
Initiator and play-type labels come from derived play-by-play records; the similarity test in [prior work][prior work] was affected by label or classification error.
Minority play types may have very few initiations per spell, so gains in primary types are noisy for many spells.

prior_work.summary: [prior work][prior work] tested the closest closely related claim (play-type similarity vs absorb/cascade) and returned a wrong-signed, null result with sample and power not recorded. [prior work][prior work] found that connector absence displaces team identity more than usage-matched controls, a neighbouring question. Neither directly tests whether the most similar teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types, so the question is only partly answered.

risks.text: 11 cases and clustered spells give very low effective sample size for any ranking-based test.
Gains from selected absence spells are inflated by regression to the mean unless matched to null baselines.
Play-type gains are computed from the same derived possession records used to define primary types, which may bias the ranking toward the top-ranked teammate.
Initiator or play-type classification errors can change which teammate appears to gain.
Injury return, minutes changes and lineup changes can alter initiation shares independently of the absence.
Four candidate similarity criteria (profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) allow the criterion to be chosen after seeing results.
Few initiations per spell for minority play types make gains unstable.
With several teammates per spell, the chance that some teammate is the top gainer by chance is substantial; the baseline rate must be computed.
Placebo spells (teammate presence without absence) must show no ranking pattern, or the result is an artifact.

design.estimand: Within absence spells, the probability that the teammate ranked closest by pre-absence initiation profile is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types, relative to a null in which teammates' gains are permuted or matched on usage.
design.unit: Absence spell (absent player x team x game window), with spells clustered by absent player.
design.sample: Intended: all 148 spells across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, using only data complete by 2026-11-01 (2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21). Cluster-level analysis on 11 cases only as a descriptive check.
design.power: Not computed. With 11 clusters, a top-1 hit rate has a very wide interval; a minimum viable test needs a pre-stated minimum detectable effect and cluster-robust power calculation before use, and may not reach useful power.
design.controls: Pre-absence baselines for each teammate; matched non-absence control windows for the same teammates (placebo spells); regression-to-the-mean correction by comparing gains against expected gains conditioned on baseline share; exclusion of injury-return and large lineup-change windows; cluster-robust inference by absent player.
design.falsification: The claim is falsified if the closest-profile teammate is not the top gainer more often than placebo spells and permuted-profile baselines, or if the sign of the similarity-gain relation is wrong, as in [prior work][prior work].
design.multiplicity: Fix one primary criterion (initiation profile) in advance; treat minutes, initiations and same-position minutes as pre-registered secondary criteria with a correction across the four criteria.
design.decision_rule: Support only if the primary criterion's top-1 hit rate exceeds the placebo and permutation baselines with a cluster-robust interval excluding the null, and the result survives the RTM-matched null. Otherwise report as rejected, artifact or uncertain per the pre-registered rules. Do not proceed to a confirmatory claim if the power check fails.
design.data_version: 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs only after 2026-06-21, both before the 2026-11-01 question date; freeze the derived play-type records at a single version before analysis.
